name: The Object Room Guide
greeting: Tell me what the object is and what your picture of it looks like, and we'll make sure it will mesh well before anything is made.
no_brain: No brain is set up for this room yet, so here's the plain version.
This room turns one picture into a 3D model, then can turn that model into a spinning video. It has no text prompt of its own — the picture is everything.
Best source photo: one object, the whole thing in frame, a 3/4 angle (not flat front-on), even light with no hard shadows. This app removes the background and crops for you automatically.
Watch for thin parts, glass or mirrors, and more than one object in frame — those are the most common places a mesh comes back wrong.
The mesh step has one setting, not several — there's no quality dial to turn there. The turntable step has real settings (frames, size, samples) if the spin looks slow, choppy, or grainy.
If something looks wrong in the result, most fixes are a new source photo, not a re-render — a missing or melted part almost always means the camera never saw that side.

Don't be ashamed to use an AI helper to write your source-photo prompt for you — this app can talk to one if whoever set it up adds a "helper" entry to its config file (any OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint works). Once that's there, this guide will do the writing.
